topic: Law change: NPPA caps trade margins at 30% of MRP for 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs; revised lower MRPs from 9 Nov 2026 (NPPA order S.O. 5690(E) dated 17 Oct 2026, Para 19, DPCO 2013)

slides.kicker: Law change · Medicine prices · From 9 Nov 2026
slides.title: Cancer medicines to get **cheaper**
slides.subtitle: Trade margins capped at **30%** on **137** anti-cancer drugs. Lower MRPs apply from **9 November 2026**.

slides.label: What changed
slides.title: A **30%** cap on trade margins
bullets: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (**NPPA**) has capped trade margins at **30% of MRP** for **137** non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs.
It covers every combination, strength and dosage form, and even **patented** medicines unless they are exempted.
NPPA used its special power under **Paragraph 19** of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013.

slides.label: How prices change
slides.title: A smaller markup, a **lower MRP**
bullets: Example: a drug sold to stockists at **₹70** with an MRP of **₹300** must now cost no more than **₹100** plus GST.
The new MRP is worked out from the company's **March 2026** prices. If the current MRP is already lower, it stays.
slides.note: **Law fact:** In 2019, a similar 30% cap on **42** cancer drugs cut prices by up to **90%** for **526** brands.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: Not every price falls by **70%**
bullets: Prices are expected to fall by **up to 70%**. The actual cut depends on each medicine's current pricing.
Companies cannot cut **production** without NPPA's permission, and must give **six months'** notice to stop a medicine.
The list was drawn up on an **expert committee's** advice and may be **updated** from time to time.

slides.label: For patients and families
slides.title: Check the **price** you pay
bullets: From **9 November**, chemists and hospitals must charge the **reduced price** and display the revised prices.
Check prices on the **Pharma Sahi Daam** app or the NPPA website. Overcharging can be reported to **NPPA**.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Cancer treatment in India is set to become cheaper from 9 November 2026 💊⚖️

The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has capped trade margins at 30% of the MRP for 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs. The cap covers every combination, strength and dosage form of these drugs, including patented medicines unless they are exempted. NPPA used its special power under Paragraph 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, on the advice of an expert committee.

What does this mean for your bill? The new MRP is based on what the company charged stockists in March 2026. For example, a drug sold to stockists at ₹70 with an MRP of ₹300 must now cost no more than ₹100 plus GST. Prices are expected to fall by up to 70%, but the actual cut depends on each medicine. If the current MRP is already lower, it stays. In 2019, a similar cap on 42 cancer drugs cut prices by up to 90% for 526 brands.

From 9 November, chemists and hospitals must charge the reduced price and display revised prices. You can check prices on the Pharma Sahi Daam app or the NPPA website, and overcharging can be reported to NPPA. Companies also cannot cut production without NPPA's permission.

Source: NPPA order S.O. 5690(E) dated 17 October 2026, under Paragraph 19, Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013

This post is for information only, not legal advice.
